title: Binomial pricing and American exercise
objectives: Derive two-state risk-neutral weights from replication/no-arbitrage and compute bounded European backward induction under explicit no-dividend per-period gross-return assumptions.
Compare continuation with intrinsic payoff at each allowed exercise node, distinguishing finite-grid American-style approximation,European rights and real-world probability/model limits.
Build the public CRR factors and exercise-enabled put recurrence at N<=1000 while preserving grid, probability, units and in-place update invariants.
motivation: One stock starts at S>0. Each period multiplies by fixed u or d, with 0<d<a<u, where a>0 is the risk-free money-market GROSS return per period.

blocks.md: One stock starts at S>0. Each period multiplies by fixed u or d, with 0<d<a<u, where a>0 is the risk-free money-market GROSS return per period. There are no dividends, fees, bid-ask spread, taxes, default, position constraints or borrowing/lending rate differences; fractional stock and borrowing/shorting needed for replication are allowed. Rates and factors are deterministic and identical across nodes. These are model assumptions, not descriptions of all markets. With annual continuous rate r and period length h years, a=exp(r*h);a simple per-period rate R would instead mean a=1+R.

For one-period payoff V_u,V_d, choose stock holding Delta=(V_u-V_d)/(S*(u-d)) and initial money-market amount B=(u*V_d-d*V_u)/(a*(u-d)). Then Delta*S*u+B*a =V_u and Delta*S*d+B*a=V_d. Under the model's no-arbitrage replication argument, the initial claim value is Delta*S+B. Rearranging gives V=((1-p)*V_d+p*V_u)/a, with p=(a-d)/(u-d). Strict d<a<u ensures 0<p<1. Do not clip invalid p into [0,1] and silently claim a valid tree.

blocks.title: A pricing weight is not the physical up chance
items: S 100, K 100, u 1.2, d 0.8, a 1. A one-step call pays 20 up, 0 down. Delta=(20-0)/(120-80)=0.5 and B=-40. Replication costs 0.5*100-40=10.
p=(1-0.8)/(1.2-0.8)=0.5, so discounted weighted payoff=(0.5*20+0.5*0)/1=10. This weight follows the model's traded returns; it is not a forecast that the stock rises 50% of the time.
Two steps have stock nodes 64,96,144 and put payoffs 36,4,0. At a 1, p 0.5, European put value=(36+2*4+0)/4=11. Count the two paths to 96; node count is not path probability.

blocks.md: At maturity n, call payoff is max(S-K,0), put payoff max(K-S,0). Node (level,j) has price S0*u^j*d^(level-j), with j up moves. European backward induction averages next down/up values with weights 1-p,p and divides by a. For exercise allowed at each tree date, replace continuation by max(intrinsic,continuation). At terminal time both use payoff. At steps 0, this own function returns immediate payoff while still validating its supplied model parameters. A path-dependent payoff generally needs extra state; terminal stock alone is insufficient.

blocks.caption: Expected exact Fraction outputs: 10; 11; 11; 450/11; 50. Requires Fraction objects for positive spot, strike, u, d, a<=10000, strict d<a<u, steps exact int 0..16, kind call/put, american exact bool. Fraction arithmetic is exact for these rational inputs; this is a generic finite binomial model, not calibrated CRR volatility, calendar or dividend implementation. App Fraction/Python capability still needs actual runner verification; no live market/account calls.

blocks.md: Take S 50, K 100, u 1.2, d 0.8, a 1.1, one period. Future put pays 40 up, 60 down; p=(1.1-0.8)/0.4=0.75. Continuation=(0.75*40+0.25*60)/1.1=450/11, about 40.9091. Immediate put payoff 50 is greater, so exercise-enabled value 50. The otherwise identical European put cannot exercise now and remains 450/11. At a 1 in the earlier two-step example, both put values equal 11: the extra right need not produce a STRICT premium.

American exercise means the contractual right to exercise before expiration;European exercise is at expiration. Our finite model permits exercise only at the listed tree dates, so it is a finite-grid approximation to continuously available American exercise, or an exact model of those discrete opportunities. American-enabled value is at least European under identical model inputs because holding remains an available choice. Do not generalize a no-dividend, nonnegative-rate call no-early-exercise result to dividends, negative rates, frictions or different settlement contracts. This lesson uses the actual max comparison instead of an unconditional shortcut.

The risk-neutral weight makes p*u+(1-p)*d=a. It prices replicable claims under the stated frictionless model without using the stock's physical expected return. It is not an estimate of profit chance, and no-arbitrage within two states does not prove the real market follows those states or that execution permits the hedge. Negative per-period interest corresponds to 0<a<1 and is admitted when strict d<a<u still holds. Do not replace that with an assumption a>=1 unless the theorem or interface explicitly requires it.

The code stores one level, then builds a NEW previous-level vector, so updating one node cannot overwrite a child still needed by another. It visits O(n^2) nodes with O(n) stored values; exact rational numerator/denominator bit costs can grow with n, so these are node-count bounds, not constant-time arithmetic promises. Exponentiation uses exact positive factors. Steps<=16 and input bounds limit teaching work, but arbitrary tiny Fraction denominators are not a hostile-input resource budget. A deployed service would need payload/bit-size limits and runtime controls separately.

Independent transfer: compare the rolling tree with a recursive full binary-tree evaluator on small n. Check European call-put parity C-P=S-K/a^n under this no-dividend model, American>=European, terminal payoff at n 0, and the early-exercise put example. Test a outside (d,u), u=d, nonpositive factors, bool steps, unsupported kind and wrong numeric types. A dividend/fee/funding or path-dependent extension changes state/recurrence assumptions; write its model and independent fixtures before changing a formula. Exact arithmetic does not establish calibration, convergence to a continuous model or trading competence.

Sources: [MIT 18.642 lecture 21 risk-neutral replication](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-642-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2024/mit18_642_f24_lec21.pdf), [Columbia binomial replication/backward induction](https://www.columbia.edu/~ks20/4106-18-Fall/BLM.pdf), [UT American exercise-versus-continuation discussion](https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/mcudina/binomial_american.pdf), [CME model/exercise/carry distinctions](https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/pubsub/pages/457083416/SPAN+Risk+Manager+-+Option+Pricing+Models). Original PDF pixels were reviewed;UT page 2 has a typo in its displayed call expression, which is not reproduced here. Its intrinsic-payoff bullet and page 3 description, plus replication and independent tests, ground the correct exercise comparison.

Extend the exact toy model with a declared CRR grid

The earlier price_tree accepts exact rational factors and steps<=16. This practice function instead receives S,K,r,sigma,T,N with ordinary floats and N<=1000. Use dt=T/N, u=exp(sigma*sqrt(dt)), d=1/u, growth=exp(r*dt), q=(growth-d)/(u-d), discount=exp(-r*dt). Annual r is continuous decimal rate, sigma is annualized decimal volatility and T is years. The guaranteed 0<q<1 is the no-arbitrage interval; it is not an estimated physical up probability. Do not clamp a bad q into range or silently broaden the old helper.

One row of values and a safe overwrite direction

At maturity j up moves give stock S*u^j*d^(N-j) and payoff max(K-stock,0). At level i,j, continuation=discount*(q*next[j+1]+(1-q)*next[j]); value=max(0,K-node_stock,continuation). The code rewrites j in INCREASING order: when writing values[j], both old children values[j] and values[j+1] are still available. Decreasing order would read an overwritten up-child. Entries beyond the new row length are ignored. This is exercise at tree dates, not a continuous-time early-exercise solver.

Compute node stocks without multiplying competing huge powers

Because d=1/u mathematically, node stock can be evaluated as S*exp((2*j-i)*sigma*sqrt(dt)). This avoids separately computing u^j and d^(i-j), whose intermediate factors can overflow even when their product is finite. The public bounds give maximum absolute node log-factor sigma*sqrt(T*N)<=100, so exp is finite here. This is algebraically the same tree with an explicit floating evaluation choice, not a claim of bitwise equality to every power library. Tests must compare the displayed answer against an independent higher-precision tree away from stated ties.

Trace, cost and rights

S=K=100,r=.05,sigma=.2,T=1,N=3 gives 6.499560. At every node the holder can keep the option, so its value is at least the immediate put payoff and at least the otherwise identical European tree. O(N^2) node work and O(N) value memory meet N<=1000; there is no exponential path enumeration in this implementation. Test one-step exercise versus continuation, deep in/out of money, zero rate, near-edge valid q and maximum N. Increasing N need not make successive grid prices monotone. Grid convergence and market model fit are different questions; no account exercise/trading action follows.

blocks.code:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math
from fractions import Fraction

def american_put(S, K, r, sigma, T, N):
    dt = T / N
    log_up = sigma * math.sqrt(dt)
    up = math.exp(log_up)
    down = 1 / up
    q = (math.exp(r * dt) - down) / (up - down)
    discount = math.exp(-r * dt)
    values = [max(K - S * math.exp((2 * j - N) * log_up), 0.0) for j in range(N + 1)]
    for level in range(N - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(level + 1):
            continuation = discount * (q * values[j + 1] + (1 - q) * values[j])
            intrinsic = K - S * math.exp((2 * j - level) * log_up)
            values[j] = max(0.0, intrinsic, continuation)
    return [f'{values[0]:.6f}']

print(*american_put(100.0,100.0,.05,.2,1.0,3))

guidedExercise.prompt: Why can a finite exercise-enabled tree be internally exact yet not equal a real American option's observed price?
guidedExercise.solution: It assumes fixed states/returns, no dividends/frictions/default, replication access and a finite exercise grid; real calibration, continuous opportunities, settlement, costs and liquidity can differ. Exact rational recurrence verifies that model, not market fit. Need explicit versioned inputs, convergence/sensitivity and contract validation.

Backward induction compares alternatives, not simultaneous payments. (The holder can choose to hold or exercise at allowed dates.)
p 0.5 weights payoff 20 and 0, with no growth discount at a 1.
